To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(i) minhash signatures are an effective compression method for social networks; and (ii) Locality Sensitive hashing allows rapid queries of compressed graphs.

(1) we can compress a social graph using minhash signatures, (2) we can rapidly search the compressed graph using LSH, (3) we can construct local communities using a simple greedy algorithm, and (4) the combination of these techniques can be deployed in software that allows interactive exploration of large social graphs.

we present an interactive method for real-time community detection in large social graphs that runs on standard laptops, and that we show that the aggregate actions and interests of large numbers of social network users can be compressed and used for interactive queries.

the aggregate behavior of large numbers of social network users can be represented by a data structure that is much smaller than the original social graph and can be processed in real-time on laptops.
